sources.dose: Modelling study: 10 experienced strength athletes performed 21 flat barbell bench variations — grip widths of 1, 1.5 and 2 biacromial widths (BAW); shoulder abduction angles 45, 70 and 90 degrees; scapula neutral, retracted, released. sources.title: The use of lifting straps during snatch alters muscle activation patterns (Lemus et al., Int J Sports Sci Coach 2025, doi 10.1177/17479541241296023)
sources.claim: Grip aids do change recruitment, but modestly and in opposite directions. Lifting straps de-loaded forearm musculature by 16.0% during the first pull of the snatch, with biceps brachii showing the greatest de-load (-8.0%) and flexor carpi radialis -1.1%, while latissimus dorsi activation rose 17.2%
sources.dose: Straps: forearm musculature -16.0% (first pull, snatch), biceps brachii -8.0%, FCR -1.1%, latissimus dorsi +17.2%. Fat/thick grips: significant increases in forearm flexor and biceps brachii activity (p<0.01), with reduced maximal repetitions. Practical rule: use straps on heavy holds/pulls during a symptomatic phase; do not use fat grips.
